items.title: Dual Entity Compliance
items.text: Expert handling of distinct labor codes for FBiH and RS.

items.title: Probation Periods
items.text: Statutory maximum of 6 months; termination during probation requires 7 days' notice.

items.title: Paid Leave
items.text: Minimum 20 working days per year, with 12 days to be taken consecutively.

items.title: Speed to Market
items.text: Onboard employees in days without establishing a DOO.

faqs.question: Is EOR legal in Bosnia?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is a common practice for engaging talent without a local entity.

faqs.question: Can I hire in both FBiH and RS?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the EOR partner must handle the specific regulations for each entity.

faqs.question: What is the notice period?
faqs.answer: Typically 15-30 days, depending on tenure and contract terms.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.text: 12+ holidays varying by entity, including religious holidays for different faiths. Key holidays include New Year's Day, Independence Day (FBiH), and Statehood Day (FBiH).

items.title: Minimum Wage
items.text: Approx. 1,000 BAM (FBiH) / 900 BAM (RS) net per month (2024). This is subject to annual adjustments by the respective entity governments.

items.title: Severance Pay
items.text: Employees heavily protected. Severance is mandatory for redundancy, often calculated as 1/3 of average monthly salary per year of service.

items.title: Work Week
items.text: Standard 40-hour work week, typically Monday to Friday. Overtime is capped and must be paid at a premium.

steps.title: Data Collection
steps.description: Collect timesheets and variable pay data.

steps.title: Entity Calculation
steps.description: Apply FBiH or RS specific tax rates and social security logic.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net
steps.description: Calculate net pay after all deductions.

steps.title: Filing
steps.description: Submit monthly reports (e.g., MIP-1023 in FBiH) to authorities.

steps.title: Payment
steps.description: Disburse net salaries and tax payments.

items.title: Dual Systems
items.text: Separate calculations for FBiH and RS employees are mandatory.

items.title: Pay Slips
items.text: Mandatory issuance of detailed pay slips to employees each month.

items.title: Bonuses
items.text: 13th-month pay is not statutory but often included in collective agreements.

faqs.question: When are taxes due?
faqs.answer: Typically monthly by the 10th or 15th of the following month. Late filings attract penalties.

faqs.question: What currency is used?
faqs.answer: Statutory payments must be made in Convertible Marks (BAM). Foreign currency payments for local salaries are generally not permitted.

faqs.question: Is RS different from FBiH?
faqs.answer: Yes, RS has a gross salary concept that includes all contributions, while FBiH splits them. This affects how you calculate total employer cost.

faqs.question: Are there 13th month salaries?
faqs.answer: Not statutory, but customary in some industries and often included in collective bargaining agreements.

items.title: Allowances
items.text: Meal and transport allowances are common and may have tax benefits.

items.title: Currency Peg
items.text: BAM is pegged to the Euro.

items.title: Banking
items.text: Employees must have a local bank account for salary deposits.

faqs.answer: FBiH and RS have completely different social security formulas.

faqs.question: Are allowances taxable?
faqs.answer: Generally no, up to certain limits defined by law.

faqs.question: How often do rates change?
faqs.answer: Rates subject to annual review; verify current status.

items.title: Updates

heroData.title: Incorporation in Bosnia and Herzegovina

steps.title: Founding Act
steps.description: Draft and notarize the Act of Establishment or Articles of Association.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Open a temporary bank account and deposit the minimum share capital.

steps.title: Court Registration
steps.description: Submit documents to the Municipal Court registry in the relevant entity.

steps.description: Register for ID number, Customs, and VAT (if applicable).

steps.title: Bank Account
steps.description: Convert temporary account to permanent corporate account.

items.title: DOO (LLC)
items.text: Most common structure (Limited Liability Company). Liability is limited to the capital contribution of the owners.

items.title: Branch Office
items.text: Not a separate legal entity; taxes apply to BiH-sourced income. Easier to close than a DOO but parent fully liable.

items.title: Rep Office
items.text: Cannot conduct commercial activities. strictly for market research and promotion.

items.title: Directors
items.text: At least one director required, no residency restriction. The director acts as the legal representative.

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: Typically 30-45 days for full incorporation and tax registration.

faqs.question: Can I open a bank account remotely?
faqs.answer: Difficult. Usually requires physical presence or strict Power of Attorney.

faqs.question: Is VAT mandatory?
faqs.answer: Mandatory if annual turnover exceeds 50,000 BAM.

items.title: Corporate Seal
items.text: A physical company stamp/seal is still widely used and often required.

items.title: Virtual Office
items.text: Allowed for registered address purposes.

items.title: Language
items.text: Docs must be in Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian (Cyrillic in RS, Latin in FBiH/RS).

items.title: Fixed Assets

items.title: Petty Cash

faqs.question: Are internal rulebooks mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, for employers with >15 (FBiH) or >30 (RS) employees. They must regulate salaries, organization, and discipline.

faqs.question: What involves safety compliance?
faqs.answer: Risk assessments (Akt o procjeni rizika) and safety training are mandatory for all employees.

faqs.question: Is whistleblowing protected?
faqs.answer: Yes, laws protect whistleblowers reporting corruption in RS and FBiH. Retaliation is prohibited.

faqs.question: How strictly is GDPR enforced?
faqs.answer: AZLP is becoming more active. Fines can be significant for data breaches or mishandling personal data.

faqs.question: Do I need a local director?
faqs.answer: At least one representative is required, but they do not have to be a BiH national or resident.

faqs.question: What is the statute of limitations?
faqs.answer: Dependent on the offense; typically 3-5 years for tax and labor violations.

items.text: Standard rate of 17% applies country-wide; export goods are zero-rated.

items.title: Double Tax Treaties
items.text: BiH has DTTs with many countries (e.g., UK, Germany, Turkey) to avoid double taxation. Proof of residency is required.

items.title: Local Differences
items.text: Always verify specific rules for the entity (FBiH vs RS) of operation. Tax forms and deadlines can vary slightly.

items.title: Employment
items.text: Subsidies available for hiring specialized categories of workers (e.g., first-time employees, long-term unemployed).

items.title: Tax Holidays
items.text: Export-oriented companies in FBiH may enjoy CIT holidays if they meet specific investment and export thresholds.

items.title: Expense Deductibility
items.text: Representation expenses are 50% deductible (FBiH) depending on specific rules. Documentation is key.

items.title: Capital Gains
items.text: Capital gains are generally included in the corporate income tax base and taxed at the standard CIT rate.
